lesson.title: Make human oversight effective
lesson.summary: Design oversight that a person can effectively exercise.

prerequisites.reason: A supervisor needs to interpret the output.

blocks: **Effective human oversight** is the ability of natural persons to oversee operation during use, to prevent or minimise relevant risks from intended use or foreseeable misuse. Measures must fit risk, autonomy and context.

The provider may build measures into the system where technically feasible, identify measures for the deployer to implement, or combine both. Adding a person’s name to a form is not evidence of effective oversight.
The system must enable the assigned person, as appropriate and proportionate, to understand capabilities/limitations, monitor operation and detect/address anomalies or unexpected performance.

It must support interpretation and decisions not to use it, to disregard, override or reverse outputs, and to intervene or interrupt it into a safe state. A pause button that leaves an unsafe process continuing is not the intended safeguard.
**Automation bias** is the tendency to automatically rely or over-rely on system outputs. It matters especially when AI recommendations inform human decisions.

Northbridge’s reviewer should not approve every suggestion solely because it is scored. This is a capacity and workflow problem, not evidence that the human is absent only when there is no mouse click.

Case: the named reviewer cannot see limitations, cannot challenge rankings and is penalised for stopping use. The interface’s “human approved” badge does not establish the needed oversight capabilities.

Request demonstrable interpretation, challenge, intervention and safe-stop arrangements. The deployment lesson will address who is assigned and supported; this lesson concerns what the system enables.

questions.prompt: A reviewer is named but cannot interpret, override or safely interrupt the system. Is the oversight design established?

options.reason: Oversight must be effective during use.

options.blocks: Yes; a name automatically fulfils it
options.reason: Naming alone does not provide the capabilities.

options.blocks: Yes; clicking approve replaces all controls
options.reason: Approval can coexist with ineffective oversight.
